At four o'clock I know three sailings are gone. At eleven I still don't know how many units that is, or which of them are reefers.
Six of us, a hundred and twenty calls, and every call is the same question. We rebook whoever gets through.
Last storm our biggest customer had forty trailers waiting until Saturday night, because they waited for their account manager — while a one-off customer who called at five sailed on Friday morning.
At cut-off I find nine reefers booked on a sailing with four free plugs. Then I'm the one bumping them.
Weather is weather. What I can't explain to the supermarket is that nobody told me my strawberries would sail on Saturday.
Every haulier still drives to the terminal, because nobody told them not to. At one in the morning trailers were parked on the access road.
My driver waited nineteen hours in his cab. He'd have stayed home if anyone had told him his new sailing.
Every storm someone books units that have no customs pre-lodgement. They take a slot, get refused at check-in, and the slot is gone.
Each storm the rules are reinvented by whoever is on duty. I want this to be boring.
We can't build 'be fair'. Give me rules a developer can test.
Fair is first come, first served. Anything else and my agents have to defend it on the phone.
Contract customers pay for capacity all year. In a storm they come first. Full stop.
Perishables and drivers first. The rest can wait a few hours — it won't rot.
Weather is force majeure. Show me a saving that isn't a claim we'd reject anyway.

A unit can only be planned on a sailing whose booking cut-off has not passed.
Planned lane metres never exceed the free lane metres of the sailing.
Reefers only go on a sailing with a free reefer plug.
Dangerous goods (ADR) only go on a sailing with a free ADR slot.
Oversized / project cargo only goes on a sailing with a high deck.
A unit without a customs pre-lodgement is held, not planned, until the pre-lodgement exists.
Class 1: perishable reefers, earliest deadline first.
Class 2: accompanied units (a driver is waiting), earliest arrival first.
Contract customers have first claim on their allotment share of every recovery sailing.
Everything else: original sailing first, then original booking time (first booked, first rebooked).
A confirmed unit is never moved to a later sailing by a replan round.
The duty manager may override a unit's sailing with a reason code; R-01 to R-05 and R-13 still apply.
A unit is only planned on a sailing it can reach: at the terminal 60 minutes before departure.
A perishable unit that cannot sail before its deadline is planned as early as possible and escalated to customer service.
Scarce slots first: ADR and project units are planned before the lane metres are handed out, onto the sailings that have their slot.
When a sailing's capacity is reduced, confirmed units that no longer fit are re-planned first and escalated; R-11 protects against replans, not against a smaller ship.
